reran: cmd.sh on w3-int, w3-base and 2.13.18: 'assertion failed: Bad superClass for class Int: <none>' in the jvm phase on all three. 2.12.20 compiles the same source. 3.7.4 compiles it (with an unreachable-case warning). An ordinary variant crashes the same way on w3-base and on 2.13.12, 2.13.14 and 2.13.16.
user_impact: Code that matches Int, Char or Long literals on an `if` whose condition is a compile-time constant and whose surviving branch throws: `object Config { final val Enabled = false }` and `(if (Config.Enabled) level() else sys.error("disabled")) match { case 0 => "off"; case 1 => "on"; case _ => "other" }`. The whole file fails to compile with an assertion that names neither the match nor the flag, and it appears or disappears when the flag is flipped. Uncommon, because the `if` has to be the scrutinee itself; binding it to a val first avoids it.
fixability: clear cut: in RefChecks.transformIf keep the type of the `if` when the surviving branch is narrower, by wrapping the branch in a Typed with the If's type or by not reducing when the branch has type Nothing; or have the match translation skip the cases when the scrutinee has type Nothing. No compatibility cost: the programs do not compile today.
regression: in 2.13.0: scala/scala PR 7260 ('Defer the pattern matching phase until after refchecks', commit 967bdc120c) moved patmat behind the phase that reduces the `if`. Inferred from 2.12.20 compiling and 2.13.12 onwards crashing; releases before 2.13.11 could not be run on the JDKs installed here.
links: None in earlier waves. scala/bug 11200 has the same assertion text from a different cause and is closed; 11115 is unrelated. No ticket found for this cause.
note: The reduction the hunter did not locate is RefChecks.transformIf (RefChecks.scala:1905-1916, called at :2111): an If whose condition has a foldable constant type is replaced by the chosen branch as is. The If had type Int (the lub with Nothing); the branch `???` or `sys.error(..)` has type Nothing. Patmat now runs after refchecks, takes the scrutinee type from the tree, declares `case val x1: Nothing`, and generates the literal test as `3 == x1` (MatchCodeGen._equals). Int.== is overloaded and every alternative accepts Nothing, so resolution fails; the patmat typer does not report that error, and the tree with an error symbol reaches the back end. With an extractor pattern (`case Some(3)`) the same cause gives 'error during expansion of this match (this is a scalac bug)' instead of a crash. String and Boolean literal patterns compile because their == is not overloaded. Writing the Nothing-typed scrutinee directly (`??? match { case 3 => }`) is rejected by typer with a type mismatch, so the refchecks reduction is the only route. Programs tried: wave4 scratch gf1/a3.scala (the Config.Enabled example), a4 (Char), a5 (Long), a9 (constant true with a throw).
